Baldur's Gate 3 is an absolute masterpiece and easily one of the best RPGs ever made.

Everything about this game is incredible, from the brilliant storytelling and unforgettable characters to the deep combat system and beautifully crafted world.

The level of freedom and player choice is simply amazing. Almost every decision matters, and there are so many different ways to approach situations.

But what truly makes this game special is its unbelievable replayability. Every new playthrough can feel like a completely different adventure, with new choices, outcomes, interactions, and discoveries.

Even after spending hundreds of hours in this world, there's always something new to experience.

The attention to detail, the writing, the voice acting, and the sheer amount of content are all outstanding.

Baldur's Gate 3 isn't just a great RPG. It's a masterpiece that sets a new standard for the entire genre. An unforgettable experience and an absolute must-play!

When I started this game for the first time, I was skeptical. I've never heard so many positive responses and reviews around one game, so I was expecting a disappointment. I didn't even realise how wrong I was... 

First 10 hours BG3 feels too complicated and overflowed with information that must be used and you can't catch everything that this game gives. But that's the point... The moment when you start to understand things, mechanics, ways to counter your enemies - you taste the brilliance of this product. 

You start seeing that Baldur's Gate 3 is not just a game, it's another dimension that can give you anything you desire. Epic fights? - No problem. Interesting plot? - Sure. Multichoice in any interaction(both combat and social)? - Of course! This game has become my personal saving from problems and anxiety in irl(and still is). Even after 1k hours of gameplay I still find something new. And that's awesome. I know that you may not be a fan of such tremendous and complicated rpgs like Baldur's Gate 3 and won't insist on playing as much as I do, but I definitely recommend you to give it a shot. As long as you proceed, the game will give you emotions you didn't expect. Hope this review was helpful. Good luck to you, adventurer! 

P. S. May gods have mercy on your enemies, 'cause you won't. Then and only then... Father will be proud...

Before writing any review, I wanted to finish the game properly. And that took me over 150 hours; 150 absolutely AMAZING hours of adventure, filled with unforgettable moments and so many positive emotions.

When I first started playing and got into my first battle, I wasn't exactly impressed. The turn-based combat system didn't convince me at all. I guess nostalgia for the good old combat system from Baldur's Gate 1 and 2 was simply too strong. But I decided to give it a chance, and once I got used to it, I realised it actually adds a whole new dimension to the game.

The same goes for the party size. Having only four characters instead of the six we had in BG1 and BG2 was initially a bit disappointing. Again, nostalgia talking. But after spending some time with the game, I realised just how brilliantly balanced the four-character party actually is. It adds another layer of complexity, forces you to think more tactically, make better use of every character's abilities, and really get the most out of your party.

And then there's everything else... The depth of the game. The seemingly endless possibilities. The decisions and their consequences. The dialogue. The incredible characters and their personal stories.

And this is where the game truly shines. Every major character you meet, especially your companions, has an incredibly detailed story of their own, one you can gradually uncover and become deeply involved in. But what makes it so special is that you're not just watching their stories unfold. You're actively shaping them. Depending on your choices, their personalities, relationships, beliefs and ultimately their fates can change dramatically. Who they become and where their stories lead is, to a remarkable extent, in your hands.

And those decisions don't exist in isolation. They have consequences, sometimes immediate, sometimes much later when you least expect them. They shape your companions, your relationships, the dynamics of your party and ultimately your entire gameplay experience. It's this incredible sense that your choices genuinely matter that makes the world feel so alive and every playthrough so personal. And, of course, a wonderful dose of nostalgia when Jaheira and Minsc showed up. Seeing those two again was something special... #corememoriesunlocked. :)

To spare you another essay, I'll get straight to the point:  This game, without a single doubt, is the best RPG I've ever played and easily among my top three games of all time. And the best part? After finishing my first playthrough, I'm already excited about what comes next. Honour Mode, different origin characters, different choices, different approaches, and all the things I haven't even discovered yet. 
In fact, I've already started my second playthrough. And despite knowing that the main storyline remains the same, thanks to the incredible variety of possibilities, it already feels like I'm playing an entirely new game.

So here's to another 150, 300, or even 500 hours of adventure. And somehow, I have a feeling even that might not be enough. :) AN ABSOLUTE MASTERPIECE!!! 100/10!

I enjoy Roleplay, I love Dungeon and Dragons, sadly, both these things are streamlined here, I certainly understand that, they wish to appeal to a bigger crowd. So if you are like me, totally into RPG, branching story, the world, story and people in it changing according to your decisions, you will be disappointed, at some point, it feels shallow.

I did play the Pathfinder games, especially Wrath of the Righteous, and as a Roleplayer, I found exactly what I was looking for there, sure, you have to read a lot, it does not look as fancy, but it is filled with content, you can be good, the hero, you can be the most evil monster consuming the world, and both paths are filled with story, the world and people change, and there are so many different classes and paths you can take in between, you can feel the game was made by true Roleplayers, for Roleplayers.

As a Roleplayer at heart, I cannot recommend Baldurs Gate 3, if you are into looks, action, shallow Roleplay and watered down D&D experience, I am sure you gonna love this one.
